li.span: Policies will be defined per zones (i.e. per cluster) and per product, and there will be a couple of per zones global policies (applied to all products)
Prod zones will get a policies in enforced mode
Non-Prod zones will get a policy in enforced or audit mode, depending on the controls applied

li.span: Actual naming rules not taken into account in this diagram for clarity's sake. Actual policy name would rather be <product>-<productId>-<env scope>-<type>-<OS>.
Specifying the clusters at the policy level rather than at the application scope level allows to only have a single application scope per product.
This design supports a distinct policy per env, or grouping a single policy for multiple envs, based on the kubernetes.cluster-??? scope criteria
Using the cluster names as a scope criteria implies that names are properly specified in Kube enforcer configurations (helm chart), and a kube enforcer is deployed on each cluster.
the exact cluster scopes we want to use. Strictly per env? Prod vs non-Prod ? Revenue generation vs non-revenue generation? sut/lrn/eng/cus? Where does UAT stand?

Depending on cluster usages and required scopes, we can try to simplify scope definition by adding prefixes to cluster names, and referring to these prefixes in scopes instead of listing all cluster names

span.font: Kube Enforcer deployments: GitOps PP and current domain model can't support this use case:

li.font: tenant specific clusters (ongoing work the accomodate this in the domain model)
